subject: Nov metrics flags & QBR prep: action plan and owners
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Nov metrics flags & QBR prep: action plan and owners

Team —

Attached is the month-end snapshot (Nov2026_KPI_dashboard.pdf). Wanted to call out three items I think we need to own ahead of the QBR and align on slides / owners:

1) Latency spike (p50/p95 drift) — looks correlated with a Gen-heavy customer workload on 11/18–11/22; backend queueing up on a subset of GPU pools. Marcus, can you and infra confirm whether the kernel selection changes rolled on 11/18 contributed?

2) Cost per 1k token — up ~18% month-over-month driven by higher long-sequence generation and a small increase in retry rates. Markus, can you run a quick economics slide showing unit cost delta and potential mitigation (quantization candidates)?

3) Minor uptime incident on 11/24 (control plane failover) — no data loss but 6m of degraded routing for a subset of customers in us-west. Laura, please summarize customer impact and any support escalations (EMail thread from ACME attached).

Action request: please review the attached dashboard and reply with a single-line owner assignment for a QBR slide by EOD Thursday (11/26). I created a shared folder for slide assets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQBR-Nov-2026.

Attachments: [Attachment: Nov2026_KPI_dashboard.pdf (PDF, 2.4MB)]

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nov metrics flags & QBR prep: action plan and owners

Neha —

Thanks for the heads up and the dashboard. I pulled a latency breakdown (attached latency-breakdown.csv) and started correlating with the kernel rollout log. Quick notes:
- We did a staged kernel swap 11/17–11/19 for the attention optimization. The rollout completed on 11/19 for 3 of 5 pools; one pool reverted automatically due to elevated retry rates.
- The p95 increase lines up with the reverted pool becoming overloaded around 11/20 as traffic rebalanced.

Short answer: likely related, but we need the infra logs to confirm cache/queue impacts (I’ll ask infra for the queue-depth histograms).

Owner for latency slide: Marcus Lin — I’ll draft a two-slide explanation (root cause + proposed mitigations) by Friday morning.

Attachment: [Attachment: latency-breakdown.csv (CSV)]

Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nov metrics flags & QBR prep: action plan and owners

Neha / all —

Summary for the QBR slide (customer impact):
- ACME reported increased latency for their heavy-gen job on 11/21; they created a support ticket and our on-call engaged — root cause tracked to traffic rebalance after the kernel rollout partial completion.
- Actual customer impact: intermittent 10–30s request slowdowns for ~120 requests (0.003% of ACME daily volume) between 11/20 02:00–11/21 04:00 PST. No data loss, no retries logged at their side, but they asked for credits as a goodwill gesture.
- We provided a timeline and mitigation steps; Emily is looped on this thread for any follow-ups.

Owner for customer-impact slide: Laura Bennett — I’ll include the timeline and the recommended credit ask amount (TBD with finance).

Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nov metrics flags & QBR prep: action plan and owners

All —

I’ll own the cost slide. Quick notes:
- I ran a baseline comparison: cost per 1k tokens rose ~18% MoM; ~11% attributed to higher average sequence length, ~7% to increased retries and fallback to more expensive model variants during the kernel instability window.
- Short mitigation options: tighter routing (short-term), enable mixed-precision quantization for a sample set of models (mid-term), and demand-based scheduling for batch windows (longer-term).

I’ll put numbers into a spreadsheet and dump a draft slide into the shared folder by Friday EOD.

Thanks team — solid owners assigned. I created a tiny workbook (QBR_slide_owners.xlsx) that maps slides to owners and slide deadlines. Please confirm the below and I’ll lock the deck:

- Latency root cause + mitigations — Marcus Lin — draft due Fri 11/27 11:00 PST (received)
- Customer impact / credits — Laura Bennett — draft due Fri 11/27 13:00 PST (received)
- Cost economics + mitigation roadmap — Markus Klein — draft due Fri 11/27 18:00 PST (pending)

A couple of open asks:
- Marcus: please include a brief rollback plan in your slide in case kernel behavior regresses during the canary.
- Markus: can you estimate the near-term savings if we enable mixed-precision quant for the top 10 heavy-gen models? Even rough numbers are fine for the QBR.

I’ll consolidate and circulate the working deck to execs on Monday morning. Drive link again: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQBR-Nov-2026

Attachment: [Attachment: QBR_slide_owners.xlsx (XLSX)]
